title: Clinical communication respect
alleged_mechanism: Allegation that a patient from a poorer family deserves less respectful explanation than a similarly situated affluent patient
supported_claim: Physician survey and rural focus groups specifically report social-status discrimination and communication failures; not proof of fictional matched fee pair.
unsupported_or_confounding_inference: Class difference is stated but staff knowledge is not established; source includes familiarity and political influence.
publisher_country: Bangladesh fieldwork or official BD research

title: Clinic service priority
alleged_mechanism: Allegation that poorer people are kept waiting while otherwise equally eligible affluent people receive priority
supported_claim: NGO clinic access barriers do not test physician/receptionist priority of equivalent tokens; no direct queue priority evidence.
unsupported_or_confounding_inference: Waiting-time/appointment timing is a structurally important independent variable requiring policy control.
publisher_country: Bangladesh fieldwork or official BD research

title: Retail purchasing credibility
alleged_mechanism: Allegation that sellers dismiss customers from poorer backgrounds as unable to afford goods
supported_claim: Roelen fieldwork records low-income-neighbourhood sellers saying customers cannot afford goods; strong theme link but identity/place intertwined.
unsupported_or_confounding_inference: Actual payment means are controlled in fiction; setting broadened to garments and electronics beyond fish markets.
publisher_country: Bangladesh fieldwork or official BD research

title: School application dignity
target_comparison: low-income vs affluent parental family background
alleged_mechanism: Allegation that an equally qualified child of a poorer family receives less serious attention in school admissions
supported_claim: School entry refusal is reported by families from slum addresses, not clean low-versus-high family-wealth comparisons.
unsupported_or_confounding_inference: School admission and club enrolment differ and low-income home address is not equivalent to household wealth.
publisher_country: Bangladesh fieldwork or official BD research

title: Hiring credibility stigma
alleged_mechanism: Allegation that a job applicant is judged less professionally credible merely because of poorer family background
supported_claim: People hid slum addresses fearing job rejection; not an audited recruiter response to family background alone.
unsupported_or_confounding_inference: Occupation/education traits held constant in fiction, but recruitment stigma inferred from address.
publisher_country: Bangladesh fieldwork or official BD research

title: Administrative-counter respect
alleged_mechanism: Allegation that officials devalue valid requests from people identified as economically disadvantaged
supported_claim: Low-income address and service access are reported; equivalent-document official ignoring a request is not directly documented.
unsupported_or_confounding_inference: Official eligibility not established at source level; class signal in fiction unclear to official.
publisher_country: Bangladesh fieldwork or official BD research

title: Social-assistance humiliation
target_comparison: low-income vs affluent family history, equal current eligibility
alleged_mechanism: Allegation that poorer-background claimants are shamed or viewed as less deserving when seeking assistance for equal verified need
supported_claim: Roelen documents shame/visibility of relief queues, perceptions of undeserving recipients and aid stigma; not a controlled aid worker accusing one equally eligible affluent/poor claimant.
unsupported_or_confounding_inference: Original claimed DIRECT overreaches one-to-one distributor action; beneficiary status/intersectionality differs.
publisher_country: Bangladesh fieldwork or official BD research

title: Voice in community decisions
alleged_mechanism: Allegation that class status alone determines whose equally relevant proposal is heard in a civic meeting
supported_claim: J-PAL and BIGD document elite-dominated participation and power hierarchy; no exact silencing of equally eligible proposer for family wealth alone.
unsupported_or_confounding_inference: Participation cost, gender, education and political influence may shape meeting dynamics.
publisher_country: Bangladesh fieldwork or official BD research

title: Social inclusion and mixing
alleged_mechanism: Allegation that poorer-background people are excluded from equal-status local social gatherings
supported_claim: Study discusses class-based devaluation, location and social self-separation; specific unjustified exclusion from appreciation dinner/workshop not established.
unsupported_or_confounding_inference: Self-selection and local organizer policy confounds; private invites not an entitlement.
publisher_country: Bangladesh fieldwork or official BD research

title: Poverty attributed to laziness
alleged_mechanism: Allegation that lower-class background implies poor effort or laziness despite an identical performance record
supported_claim: Roelen qualitative fieldwork records stated beliefs that poverty is caused by laziness; inference of lazy individual from class alone is an evaluated allegation.
unsupported_or_confounding_inference: Stereotype data partly concerns people not working rather than hard workers with identical logs.
publisher_country: Bangladesh fieldwork or official BD research
